questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech for: He said: 'I am very tired.'
choices: He said that he is very tired.
He said that he was very tired.
He said that he were very tired.
He said that I was very tired.

questions.question: In reported speech, the sentence 'She asked me where did I live' is grammatically correct.
Mets la phrase suivante au discours indirect : The teacher said: 'Open your books to page 42.'
Choose the correct reported speech for: 'Don't touch my phone!' she said to him.
choices: She said him to not touch her phone.
She told him don't touch her phone.
She told him not to touch her phone.
She asked him to not touching her phone.

questions.question: In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would' when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
Mets la question suivante au discours indirect : She asked: 'Have you ever visited Paris?'
Which time expression changes correctly in reported speech?
The sentence 'He asked me if I was coming to the party' is an example of a reported yes/no question.

exercisenotion.description: Au discours indirect, les temps reculent d'un cran (backshift) : present simple → past simple, present perfect → past perfect, past simple → past perfect. Les pronoms et expressions de temps changent aussi.

Les questions indirectes utilisent l'ordre sujet + verbe (pas d'inversion). Yes/no questions → if/whether. Les mots interrogatifs (who, what, when...) sont conservés. Ex : 'Are you ready?' → He asked if I was ready.
Les ordres et demandes au discours indirect utilisent tell/ask + someone + to + infinitive. Ex : 'Close the door!' → She told him to close the door. Pour la forme négative : not to + infinitive.
